$comment: MACHINE-READABLE RULES REQUIREMENT — HANDOFF, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION.,This repository does not own a canonical firestore.rules file: firebase.json here has no,'firestore' section, and .emulator-local/firestore.rules is untracked local scratch (it also,still contains a God-Mode identity backdoor and a status denylist, and must not be treated as,the contract). The rules owner is the mobile/backend lane. This file states exactly what those,rules must enforce and how to test it, so the requirement can be applied without re-deriving it.,Nothing here has been deployed, and no rules file has been modified by this lane.,v2.0.0 strengthens this from a description into a machine-verifiable contract:,every collection now declares its permitted server projection, the role/status required to,reach it through a callable, and the aliases/alternate paths that must NOT bypass it.,scripts/outreach-production-binding-verify.mjs enforces the parts that are checkable from,this repository; the rules themselves remain the owning lane's to apply. v2.1.0 adds the three server-owned enterprise staff grant collections raised by the manageEnterpriseStaff re-review.
rationale: These five collections are SERVER-OWNED. Every read and write is performed by Cloud Functions
through the Firebase Admin SDK, which bypasses security rules entirely, so denying all direct
client access costs the product nothing and removes the entire client attack surface.
They carry approval authority (who approved what, at which version, under which digest) and
outreach draft text. A client that could write them could forge an approval; a client that
could read them could read draft content scoped to someone else.

collections.notes: Client reads must be denied even for staff: the server projection scopes draft content to the creator and assigned reviewer, and a direct read would bypass that scoping.
collections.projectionScoping: subject and body are returned ONLY to the record creator or the assigned reviewer; every other active staff member receives null for both.

collections.notes: Append-only. No client, including staff, may create, update or delete a receipt.
collections.projectionScoping: not projected to any client by any callable in this lane. No field of this record is projected to any client. The empty allowlist above is a deliberate "nothing is exposed", not an unfilled section.

carries: replay ledger: command fingerprint and stored outcome
collections.notes: A client that could write this could forge a replayed success for a command it never made.
collections.projectionScoping: internal replay ledger; never projected. No field of this record is projected to any client. The empty allowlist above is a deliberate "nothing is exposed", not an unfilled section.

collections.notes: A client write here would let a caller lift their own legal hold. Absence of a document means NOT held; a failed read means UNKNOWN and blocks.
collections.projectionScoping: exposed only as the boolean/null hold state on a draft row.

collections.notes: A client write here would manufacture legal approval for a jurisdiction counsel has not approved.
collections.projectionScoping: exposed only as a boolean on a draft row; the approval version is not projected.
collections.requiredCallerRole: Director for any future write path

collections.notes: This document IS the role grant. A client write here is a self-issued authorization. It is also the target of a collection-group query, so a rule must cover the SUBCOLLECTION scope, not only a top-level path.
collections.collectionGroupScope: members — the rule must deny at collection-group scope; a rule matching only /enterprise_staff/{a}/members/{b} does not constrain a collectionGroup query
collections.projectionScoping: No client projection exists. These records are read by the server only; nothing here is returned to a browser.
collections.requiredCallerAuthority: an active enterprise-tier b2b_partner, resolved by uid or by a VERIFIED address — not Admin staff status. Recorded here because it differs from the outreach collections above.

collections.notes: Append-only evidence that a role grant occurred, written inside the same transaction as the grant itself. A client able to create one could manufacture evidence for a grant that never happened; a client able to overwrite one could erase a grant that did. The target address is deliberately NOT stored — the uid is the identity.
collections.immutability: created with create() inside a transaction; never updated or deleted by application code
collections.projectionScoping: No client projection exists. These records are read by the server only; nothing here is returned to a browser.
collections.requiredCallerAuthority: an active enterprise-tier b2b_partner, resolved by uid or by a VERIFIED address — not Admin staff status. Recorded here because it differs from the outreach collections above.

collections.notes: The monotonic grant sequence. It lives outside the membership document precisely so that removing a member does not reset it — a reset would make the next genuine grant collide with the first audit id. A client that could lower this counter could cause a later grant to overwrite earlier evidence.
collections.immutability: monotonic; only ever increased, by the server, inside the grant transaction
collections.projectionScoping: No client projection exists. These records are read by the server only; nothing here is returned to a browser.
collections.requiredCallerAuthority: an active enterprise-tier b2b_partner, resolved by uid or by a VERIFIED address — not Admin staff status. Recorded here because it differs from the outreach collections above.

collections.notes: THE AUTHORITATIVE MEMBERSHIP BINDING. One document per principal at a known path, read directly rather than discovered by a collection-group query. It exists because collectionGroup("members") matches a subcollection NAME wherever it lives, so a members document from any other domain came back looking exactly like enterprise staff. A client able to write here could re-home itself to another enterprise.
collections.requiredCallerAuthority: an active enterprise-tier b2b_partner, resolved by uid or by a VERIFIED address — not Admin staff status.
collections.projectionScoping: No client projection exists. Read by the server only.

collections.notes: Immutable evidence that an authority was REVOKED, written with create() inside the same transaction as the tombstone. Removal used to be a hard delete that left no record of who removed whom, when, or why. The reason is drawn from a closed vocabulary, never free text, so this record cannot become a private note about a named person. A client able to create one could fabricate a revocation; one able to overwrite one could hide a real removal.
collections.requiredCallerAuthority: an active enterprise-tier b2b_partner whose membership binding still matches the target at the moment of removal.
collections.immutability: created with create() inside a transaction; never updated or deleted by application code. The document id carries the caller-supplied commandId, which is what makes an exact replay idempotent and an altered replay refusable.
collections.projectionScoping: No client projection exists. Read by the server only.

requiredRule.form: explicit deny for every operation, placed so no earlier broader match can grant access
requiredRule.placement: Must not be shadowed by a preceding wildcard match such as /{document=**} that allows staff reads. Verify with the rules simulator that an authenticated staff account is denied.

testContract.notes: Staff too. The callable is the only authorized path, because it applies content scoping.
A direct write would bypass the digest, version and separation-of-duties checks.
Receipts are append-only; deletion must be impossible from any client.
Forging a ledger entry would let a caller be served a success for a command never made.
Otherwise a caller can lift the hold that blocks them.
Legal approval is not a thing any client may assert.
Admin SDK bypasses rules by design; this entry records the intended server path, not a rule to write.
A single-path match rule does not cover collection-group reads; this needs its own denial.
A nested copy must not be readable.
Suspended staff have no path at all, callable or direct.
The legacy shape the old denylist admitted must be denied here too.

verifiedByThisLane.notes: Both properties are asserted on every gate run. This lane cannot verify the rules themselves, because it does not own a rules file.

handoff.action: Apply requiredRule to the canonical firestore.rules and add testContract R1-R15 to the rules test suite. Cover the alternate paths in aliasAndAlternatePathControls.
handoff.blocking: Until applied, these collections rely solely on the absence of client code that reads them — which is a convention, not a control.

aliasAndAlternatePathControls.rationale: A deny rule on an exact collection path is bypassed by any other path that reaches the same data: a collection-group query, a differently-cased or pluralized alias, a nested subcollection, or a client constant that spells the name indirectly.

forbiddenAlternatePaths.requirement: must be denied; a collection-group query is not covered by a single-path match rule
must be denied; nesting must not create a readable copy
no such collection may be created; Firestore paths are case-sensitive so an alias is a distinct, unruled collection
client code must not construct these names at all, directly or by concatenation
no mirror may be created without extending this contract

verifiedHere: no client file names any of the five collections
no client file constructs a collection name by concatenation of the enterprise_ prefix
no collectionGroup query names any of the five collections anywhere in the repository
